candidates.text:
Before there were seasons, the Orchard held only one tree, and it bore a single fruit that never fell. Beneath it lived the first people, who did not age, for nothing in the world had yet learned how to end. They sang to the tree each morning, and it was content, until a girl named Ashe asked it why its branches were always reaching downward, as if trying to set something down. The tree, ashamed of its burden, let go. The fruit dropped into her hands, split open, and inside was not seed but silence. Ashe ate it, and by evening she lay still in the roots, and the people learned grief.

The tree wept sap for a hundred years. At last it bent low and spoke its first and only words: *I am sorry. I could not hold it forever.* Then its leaves turned grey, and from them grew every orchard since, each fruit a small and patient ending.

Before there was dying, the Orchard was crowded with everything that had ever lived. Foxes stood shoulder to shoulder with their great-great-grandmothers, and the oldest man, Ennic Who Remembered Rain, had grown so thin with years that light passed through him like water through linen. He begged the trees for rest, but the trees did not understand, for they had never needed it.

At last the eldest pear, whose roots touched the bottom of the world, took pity. It let fall a single grey fruit, and Ennic ate it and lay down in the long grass and did not rise. The others wept, and the pear trembled, for it had not known that rest would leave such an empty place. So it bowed its branches to the ground and said, "I am sorry." Ever since, the trees of the Grey Orchard drop their leaves each autumn over the graves, so that no one is ever buried uncovered, and no grief goes unanswered.

Since that day every fruit in the Grey Orchard falls in its season, and every grave is planted with a seed, so that the tree may keep apologising, and the dead may answer.
